headline: South Asia: Heavy losses reported as Yemen fighting escalates
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Heavy losses reported as Yemen fighting escalates.
- Asia: Russian strikes kill 11 across Ukraine after Zelensky warning.
- Western Russia: Satellite images reveal damage from strikes on Russian plant producing Kh-59 missile components.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: Former Air J plane bombed in Iran.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: Former Air J plane bombed in Iran.
When the Israeli Air Force reported the destruction of Iran’s presidential VIP Airbus A340-300 often dubbed ‘Iran Force One’ during a military strike in Iran in March of this year, the repercussions were felt beyond the Middle East, reaching Kingston, Jamaica. The long-range jet was once in the fleet of the now-defunct Air Jamaica. And for veteran aircraft pilot Edward Miller, who regularly captained the airplane on flights from Jamaica to London and Manchester in the United Kingdom, news of its demise hit a personal chord.
United States - bottom line: Aboard the USS George Washington, young sailors adjust to war with Iran.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Aboard the USS George Washington, young sailors adjust to war with Iran.
Sailors must maintain a ​state of alert and readiness, heightened in the case of the George Washington due to the threat of Iranian attacks.
- Military Times, one day ago: Fort Hood mass shooter Nidal Malik Hasan to die by US Army firing squad.
Hasan, a former Army officer who killed 13 people and injured 32 others during a mass shooting at Fort Hood in 2009, will be executed by firing squad.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: US Army tests counter-drone tech at Mexican border as cartel drone use rises.
The service is seeking to sharpen its defenses against the growing threat of drone use by cartels.

Russian forces launched a series of missile strikes on Pryluky in Chernihiv Oblast on the morning of 7 October, hitting an apartment building, a children and youth centre and a business.

- AllAfrica - Conflict, 7 hours ago: Sudan: Sudan's Death Toll in 2025 Could Be As High As 100,000 - How We Did the Count.
[The Conversation Africa] Estimates of the number of people directly killed in Sudan's civil war vary widely, in part because counting casualties in active conflict zones is extremely difficult. In 2025, for instance, one conflict monitoring organisation reported around 19,000 direct deaths from political violence across Sudan. Other research teams put the toll at more than 70,000.

South Asia - bottom line: Heavy losses reported as Yemen fighting escalates.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: Heavy losses reported as Yemen fighting escalates.
• 115 govt troops, 160 Houthi fighters killed in 24 hours • Rebels claim attack on Riyadh airport, deny losing territory • Riyadh claims intercepting missile • Over 184,000 people displaced by fighting • Pakistanis in Saudi Arabia urged to avoid sharing sensitive footage SANAA: Fighting across Yemen has killed more than 270 government troops and Houthi fighters over the past day, sources on both sides said on Tuesday. Houthis also claimed an attack on the Saudi capital’s main airport and on Tuesday denied being pushed back by government forces.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, 7 hours ago: US Vice President Vance says Iran must cut enrichment to end war.
US Vice President JD Vance has said in an exclusive interview with Reuters that Iran must make a meaningful reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the country’s seven-month war, even as Washington was unsure how Tehran makes decisions in negotiations. Vance, a longtime sceptic of US involvement in foreign wars, has taken a leading role in negotiating a settlement to the conflict and brokered a provisional peace agreement in June that quickly fell apart.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: In pictures: What Gaza looks like after 3 years of destruction wrought by Israel.
Three years after Hamas’s Oct 7, 2023 attack on Israel triggered a devastating onslaught, much of Gaza still lies in ruins. Deadly Israeli strikes continue despite a fragile ceasefire that has largely held for almost a year. Homes, hospitals, schools and entire neighbourhoods have been destroyed or severely damaged, while millions of Palestinians have been displaced. Here is a look at the scale of destruction and what life — rather, what remains of it — is like in Gaza today.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: 18 terrorists killed in separate engagements in KP, Balochistan: state media.
Security forces eliminated 18 terrorists in separate engagements in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, state media reported on Wednesday, citing security sources. In KP, Pakistan TV reported that security forces “killed 13 Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in North Waziristan, as operations against militant groups continue under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision”. Separately, in Balochistan’s Mastung district, security forces killed five terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan, Pakistan TV reported.

Jeff Kingston used to take long walks with his dogs across the hills of Gunma in central Japan. But not this year. He has good reason. Kingston says he has encountered bears in those mountains more than 100 times over the years and been charged by aggressive bears around a dozen times. - Times of India - Top Stories, just now: Couple paid for Bali trip, but operator left them out; commission orders Rs 90,000.
A Kerala consumer commission has mandated a tour operator to remit Rs 90,000 for failing to deliver a booked Bali tour. The consumer, who paid Rs 82,500, was excluded from the trip, prompting a partial refund that was inadequate. The commission ruled that this constituted unfair trade practices under the Consumer Protection Act, resulting in further compensation for legal expenses totaling Rs 10,000.

Rahul Gandhi stepped up his attack on Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, who has been in the opposition's crosshairs over his functioning and reported dissent among his subordinates. The Congress leader , declaring to launch a fresh protest from Jantar Mantar, said, "Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign," and called him an “illegitimate” poll body chief.
- Times of India - Top Stories, just now: UK shopper paid £1 for vase; it later sold for £484,000.
In a heartwarming tale of luck, a man acquired a simple yellow vase for just £1 at a charity shop. Upon listing it on eBay, he was inundated with inquiries, prompting him to seek expert appraisal. Experts revealed that it was an imperial piece crafted for the Qianlong Emperor, leading to a whirlwind auction. In a stunning twist, the vase fetched £484,000, transforming the man's financial fate tremendously.
